docs.title: AcademyOS Go SDK
docs.text:
The Go SDK and command line for AcademyOS. Keep a course as a course-spec directory in git, and use academyos to check it, upload it with its slide decks, translations and quizzes, and publish it.

go install github.com/academyosio/academyos-go/cmd/academyos@latest
export ACADEMYOS_API_KEY=aos_live_…
academyos course push courses/building-web-apis

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: You want to Read Install the CLI and connect it to an academy Getting Started Validate, push and publish courses Command Line Call AcademyOS from Go Go SDK Let a coding agent publish courses AI Agents Call the HTTP API from another language API Reference

docs.title: What an API key can do
docs.text: An API key belongs to one academy. With it you can create, update and publish that academy's courses, upload course packages and their files, and manage the academy's pronunciations. Enrollments, learner progress, analytics, billing and key management aren't available to API keys.

docs.title: AI Agents
docs.text:
A coding agent can keep courses in a repository and publish them with the academyos CLI. Add this to the course repository's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md:

## Publishing to AcademyOS

- Courses are course-spec directories. After every change, run
  `academyos course validate <dir>` and fix every error before pushing.
- Upload with `academyos course push <dir>`, then commit the updated
  `published.json`.
- The server and key come from ACADEMYOS_API_URL and ACADEMYOS_API_KEY.
  Never print, log, or commit the key.
- Exit code 3 means the course changed in the academy. Stop and ask before
  using --force.
- Never change a published lesson's ID (a slide's data-id with
  data-lesson); learner progress is keyed by it.
- Pronunciations shared by several courses go in the repository's root
  `pronunciations.json`; push them with `academyos pronunciations push`
  (try `--dry-run` first). A course's own `pronunciations.json` wins over
  the academy's.
- Use --format json when you need to read the output.

Every command takes --format json, and the exit codes tell an agent what to do next without reading the text.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: The API reference documents the AcademyOS HTTP API that an API key may call, for clients in any language. Download the OpenAPI 3.1 document: academyos.json.

docs.title: Server and authentication
docs.text:
Requests go to https://app.academyos.io, with the API key as a bearer token:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACADEMYOS_API_KEY" \
  https://app.academyos.io/api/v1/users/me

A key belongs to one academy, given by {orgSlug} in paths, and has courses:read or courses:write. Reading needs either; anything that changes a course or the academy's pronunciations needs courses:write.

docs.title: What it covers
docs.text:
Area Operations Identity Who the key acts for, its academy and scopes Courses List, create, read, update, delete and publish Sections and lessons Create, update, delete and reorder; read a lesson, its narration and its player Quizzes Create, read, update and delete a lesson's quiz Versions Create, read, update and publish course versions and their content updates Course packages Read and apply a course package, and upload or download its files by SHA-256 Pronunciations Read and replace the academy's pronunciations, review them, and suggest respellings

Errors use the problem format (application/problem+json) with title, status and detail.

docs.title: Where the document comes from
docs.text: The document is generated from the AcademyOS server's code: its operations are those an API key may call there, and the server's tests keep the two in step. This repository's copy is openapi/academyos.json; the SDK's tests check that every request the client makes is in it.

docs.title: Command Line
docs.text:
academyos whoami                       # who the key acts for, its academy and scopes
academyos course validate <dir>        # check a course; exits 2 on errors
academyos course push <dir>            # validate, upload what the academy lacks, apply
academyos course push --dry-run <dir>  # report what would change
academyos course publish <dir>         # publish the course
academyos pronunciations push [path]   # replace the academy's pronunciations
academyos pronunciations push --dry-run [path]  # list what would change
academyos pronunciations get           # print the academy's pronunciations
academyos version

Every command takes --format json.

docs.title: Courses
docs.text:
push uploads only files the academy doesn't have, applies the whole course in one step, and matches lessons by ID, so learners keep their progress. It writes the academy's IDs and revision to the course's published.json. Commit that file: the next push sends the revision, and if the course changed in the academy since then, the push is refused instead of overwriting those edits.

A typical push:

$ academyos course push courses/becoming-a-product-builder
checking 42 files with https://app.academyos.io
uploading 3 files
applied becoming-a-product-builder to https://app.academyos.io in productbuildershq, revision 7
  files     42 in the package, 3 uploaded
  sections  0 created, 1 updated, 4 unchanged, 0 kept, 0 removed
  lessons   1 created, 2 updated, 19 unchanged, 0 kept, 0 removed
  quizzes   0 created, 1 updated, 4 unchanged, 0 kept, 0 removed
recorded the academy's IDs in published.json

docs.title: Pronunciations
docs.text: pronunciations push sends a pronunciations.json, by default the one in the current directory, usually the course repository's root, as the academy's pronunciations. Narration applies a course's own pronunciations.json first, then the academy's, then the platform's, so a term shared by several courses belongs at the root. The push lists the terms added, changed and removed, and removes from the academy any term the file leaves out. An empty respelling says the term as written.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Failure: network, server, or usage 2 The course has validation errors 3 The academy's copy is newer, or the course exists without a package: pull first, or pass --force 4 The API key is missing, invalid, expired, or not allowed

docs.title: Install
docs.text: go install github.com/academyosio/academyos-go/cmd/academyos@latest

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Variable Meaning ACADEMYOS_API_KEY An API key, aos_live_…, created in AcademyOS by an instructor or admin. Required ACADEMYOS_API_URL The server. Default https://app.academyos.io; for a local server, http://localhost:8080

The key is read only from the environment, never from a flag. It is sent only over HTTPS, or plain HTTP to localhost. A key belongs to one academy, so commands use that academy; --org is needed only to double-check it.

docs.title: Check the key
docs.text:
academyos whoami

whoami prints who the key acts for, its academy and its scopes. A key with courses:read can read courses; courses:write can also change and publish them.

docs.title: Push a course
docs.text:
academyos course validate courses/building-web-apis
academyos course push --dry-run courses/building-web-apis
academyos course push courses/building-web-apis
academyos course publish courses/building-web-apis

Then commit the course's updated published.json. See Command Line for every command and exit code.

docs.title: Go SDK
docs.text:
go get github.com/academyosio/academyos-go
Package Purpose academyos The client: Me, Push, PublishCourse, pronunciations, and the package and file calls coursepkg The files a course-spec directory needs, with checksums and a package root that includes a shared theme

docs.title: Create a client
docs.text:
c, err := academyos.New(academyos.Options{
    APIKey: os.Getenv("ACADEMYOS_API_KEY"),
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

BaseURL defaults to https://app.academyos.io. The client refuses to send a key over plain HTTP except to localhost and loopback addresses. A Client is safe for concurrent use.

docs.title: Push and publish a course
docs.text:
res, err := c.Push(ctx, "courses/building-web-apis", academyos.PushOptions{})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Println(res.CourseID, res.Uploaded, "files uploaded")

if _, _, err := c.PublishCourse(ctx, "courses/building-web-apis", ""); err != nil {
    return err
}

PushOptions:

Field Meaning Org The academy; empty means the API key's academy DryRun Report what would change without changing anything Prune Remove sections and lessons the course no longer lists, except lessons learners have used Force Overwrite a newer copy in the academy Progress When set, told about each step

docs.title: Pronunciations
docs.text:
res, err := c.PushPronunciations(ctx, "pronunciations.json", academyos.PronunciationsOptions{DryRun: true})

GetPronunciations and PutPronunciations read and replace the academy's pronunciations directly, and DiffPronunciations compares two sets.

docs.title: Lower-level calls
docs.text:
Method Request Me GET /api/v1/users/me GetPackage, PutPackage GET, PUT /api/v1/organizations/{orgSlug}/courses/{courseSlug}/package GetFile, PutFile GET, PUT /api/v1/organizations/{orgSlug}/files/{sha256} Publish POST /api/v1/organizations/{orgSlug}/courses/{courseSlug}/publish GetPronunciations, PutPronunciations GET, PUT /api/v1/organizations/{orgSlug}/pronunciations

Each is described in the API Reference. A test checks that every request the client makes is in the reference's OpenAPI document.

docs.title: Errors
AcademyOS Go SDK and CLI: Plan
Approach
docs.text: Build the SDK and CLI against an httptest server first, so the client is finished and tested before the server endpoints exist, then switch the AcademyOS team's own courses to it. The module stays unpublished until those courses go through it to a local server and to app.academyos.io.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Module and client. Options, the base URL default and override, the HTTPS rule, typed errors, and Me.
  2. Course packages. coursepkg.Build over a course-spec directory, with the package root for shared themes and the size limits.
  3. Push. Local validation, the missing-files rounds, dry runs, prune, conflicts, and writing the academy's IDs to published.json.
  4. CLI. whoami, course validate, course push, and course publish, with text and JSON output and the exit codes.
  5. Round trip. pull and status.
  6. Prove it. Push the ProductBuildersHQ courses to a local AcademyOS, then production, by hand and through an agent.
  7. Docs and release. README with an agent guide, make the repository public, tag v0.1.0.

docs.title: Dependent Work in Other Projects
docs.text: Project Change AcademyOS GET /api/v1/me; the package and file endpoints with revisions and conflicts; applying a course-spec package with the same validation; course IDs written back in responses. Replaces the current definition endpoint and the per-deck storage in the deck playback spec. Its course commands move out of academyos-server once this CLI can push course-spec Write helpers for published.json (RMI-COURSESPEC-013), so this module and recording tools update it the same way ProductBuildersHQ courses Port to course-spec (RMI-COURSESPEC-006) before they can be pushed with this CLI

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Public module, private until proven. The repository's history is written as public from the first commit, and it is made public once the success criteria are met.
  • The academy comes from the key. Keys belong to one academy, so commands don't need --org.
  • Files, not one document. Uploading content-addressed files lets decks and their assets travel with the course, and repeats upload nothing.
  • The key only from the environment. Never a flag, so it doesn't land in shell history or process lists.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
1. Package root for a shared theme. Uploading the shared theme with each course is simple; a theme shared by several courses could later be uploaded once per academy.
  2. Device sign-in. Worth adding when authors other than us push courses.

docs.title: AcademyOS Go SDK and CLI: Product Requirements
Summary
docs.text: academyos-go is a public Go module with an SDK for the AcademyOS API and the academyos command built on it. An author, or an AI agent working for one, keeps a course as a course-spec directory in git and uses academyos to check it, upload it with its slide decks, translations, and quizzes, publish it, and see what differs from the academy. It talks to https://app.academyos.io unless told to use another server, such as one running locally.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Course authoring through the API works today, but not as a tool others can install:

  • The upload command lives in the AcademyOS server binary, so an author needs the server's code and its dependencies to push a course.
  • Its HTTP client is internal to the server, so no other Go program, such as an MCP server or a CI job, can reuse it.
  • The upload sends one JSON document with the outline and quizzes. Slide decks, translations, pronunciations, and the files decks load can't be sent at all.
  • The course format it reads is AcademyOS's own. The open course-spec format replaces it.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Install with one command. go install github.com/academyosio/academyos-go/cmd/academyos@latest, with no server code in the module.
  2. The whole course in one push. Outline, decks, the files decks load, translations, pronunciations, and quizzes, uploaded together and applied in one step on the server.
  3. Check before upload. The course is validated locally with course-spec, with the same rules the server applies, so nothing is uploaded from a broken directory.
  4. Safe to repeat and safe for agents. Pushing an unchanged course changes nothing. A push from a stale copy is refused instead of overwriting edits made in the academy. Every command has JSON output and distinct exit codes.
  5. Production by default, local on request. The default server is https://app.academyos.io; a flag or environment variable points at another, such as http://localhost:8080.
  6. One SDK for every adapter. The CLI is a thin layer over the SDK, so an MCP server and other tools later share the same calls.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Running or operating a server. Migrations, invites, and administration stay in academyos-server.
  • Signing in through a browser. The first release uses API keys created in AcademyOS; a device sign-in flow can follow.
  • An MCP server. It comes after the CLI has proven the SDK.
  • Editing courses outside course-spec. The SDK reads and writes course-spec directories.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: User Needs Course author Install, push, publish, and see what changed, without learning the API AI agent Exact commands, JSON output, actionable errors, and refusals instead of silent overwrites CI pipeline A non-interactive push on merge, configured by environment variables AcademyOS team Push our own academy's courses with the tool we give authors, to prove it before publishing the module

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• The server is https://app.academyos.io unless --api-url or ACADEMYOS_API_URL names another.
  • The API key comes from ACADEMYOS_API_KEY, never from a command-line argument, so it stays out of shell history and process lists.
  • Keys are sent only over HTTPS, except to localhost and loopback addresses for development.
  • An API key belongs to one person in one academy, so the academy comes from the key. --org is optional and must match when given.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• academyos whoami shows the key's person, academy, scopes, and expiry.
  • academyos course validate <dir> checks a course with course-spec.
  • academyos course push <dir> validates, uploads only files the server lacks, and applies the course. --dry-run reports what would change without changing anything. --prune removes sections and lessons no longer in the directory, except lessons learners have started.
  • academyos course status <dir> compares the directory with the academy: what is new, changed, or removed on each side.
  • academyos course pull <dir> writes changes made in the academy, such as edited narration, back to the directory, refusing to overwrite local edits unless forced.
  • academyos course publish <dir> publishes the course.
  • After a push, the academy's IDs for the course, lessons, and quizzes are written to the course's published.json, so a fresh clone knows what is live.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Text by default; --format json for tools and agents.
  • Exit codes distinguish success, a general failure, validation errors, a stale copy, and an authentication failure.
  • Validation errors from the server use the same finding format as course-spec, with file, location, message, and fix.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
1. A ProductBuildersHQ course, kept in course-spec format, is pushed with its decks and quizzes to a local AcademyOS and then to app.academyos.io, by a person and by an AI agent following only the README.
  2. Pushing it again unchanged reports nothing to do.
  3. Narration edited in the academy comes back with pull, and a push from the older copy is refused with a message that says to pull.
  4. go list -deps ./... in this module contains no AcademyOS server packages.
  5. After that, the repository is made public and v0.1.0 is tagged.

docs.title: AcademyOS Go SDK and CLI: Technical Requirements
Module
docs.text:
• Module path: github.com/academyosio/academyos-go.
  • Packages:
Package Purpose academyos The SDK: Client, options, typed errors, and one method per API call coursepkg Turns a course-spec directory into a package: the files it needs, their checksums, and the package root cmd/academyos The Cobra CLI, a thin layer over the SDK
  • Dependencies: github.com/academyosio/course-spec, github.com/spf13/cobra, and the standard library. No AcademyOS server packages; a test checks the dependency list.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
c, err := academyos.New(academyos.Options{
    BaseURL:    "",                          // default https://app.academyos.io
    APIKey:     os.Getenv("ACADEMYOS_API_KEY"),
    HTTPClient: nil,                         // default: a client with a timeout
    UserAgent:  "",                          // default academyos-go/<version>
})
  • BaseURL precedence in the CLI: --api-url, then ACADEMYOS_API_URL, then https://app.academyos.io.
  • New refuses a key with an http:// URL unless the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1.
  • Keys look like aos_live_…. The SDK sends Authorization: Bearer <key> and never logs the key or prints it in errors.

docs.title: Course Packages
docs.text:
A push sends the course as files, not as one JSON document, so decks, the files they load, and translations travel with the outline.

coursepkg.Build(dir) loads the course with course-spec and lists:

  • course.json, pronunciations.json, the description file, thumbnail, and certificate template;
  • each released section's section.json, quiz, and text lessons;
  • each deck, its voiceover/transcript.json, and every relative file it loads (styles, scripts, fonts, images, media);
  • the theme directory's files.

It leaves out published.json (the server writes its own IDs back through the response), build/ output, and files nothing references.

Package root. Paths in a package are relative to the package root: the course directory, or the nearest directory holding both the course and a shared theme outside it, such as courses/ for "theme": "../shared/theme". The package records the course directory's path within the root. No path may leave the root.

Manifest. The package is a list of {path, sha256, size} sorted by path, plus the course path. Its own checksum identifies the package version.

Limits match the server's: 20 MB per file, 200 MB per package, standard web media types only. Build reports a file over a limit before anything is uploaded.

docs.title: API Calls
docs.text:
The SDK uses these AcademyOS endpoints. The server side is specified with AcademyOS's deck playback work, which replaces its per-deck storage with this package design.

Call Endpoint Purpose Me GET /api/v1/users/me The key's person, academies and roles, and the key's academy, scopes, and expiry GetPackage GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/courses/{courseId}/package The current manifest and its revision PutPackage PUT /api/v1/organizations/{org}/courses/{courseId}/package Propose a manifest; returns missing checksums, or applies it PutFile PUT /api/v1/organizations/{org}/files/{sha256} Upload one file; the server checks the hash GetFile GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/files/{sha256} Download one file Publish POST /api/v1/organizations/{org}/courses/{courseId}/publish Publish the course

courseId is the course-spec ID.

docs.title: Push
docs.text:
1. Validate locally with course-spec. Errors stop the push.
  2. Build the package.
  3. PutPackage with the manifest, the revision the local copy was last synced at, and dryRun and prune flags.
  4. When the response lists missing checksums, PutFile each one, at most four at a time, then repeat step 3.
  5. The server loads the package with course-spec, applies the same validation, and updates the course in one transaction. It answers with a summary (created, updated, unchanged, kept, and removed sections, lessons, and quizzes), the new revision, and its IDs for the course, lessons, and quizzes.
  6. Write the IDs, base URL, and revision to published.json under platforms.academyos.

With dryRun, the server reports the summary without applying it, and step 6 is skipped.

docs.title: Revisions and Conflicts
docs.text:
Every applied package, and every edit made in the academy such as narration changed in review, raises the course's revision. The local copy's revision is the one in published.json.

  • A push whose revision is older than the server's is refused with 409 and the list of files that changed in the academy. The CLI says to run pull, or to pass --force to overwrite them.
  • A first push has no revision. If the course already exists in the academy, the push is refused unless --force is given, so a course isn't overwritten by an unrelated directory with the same ID.

docs.title: Pull
docs.text: GetPackage, then GetFile for each file whose checksum differs from the local file, written in place. A local file that changed since the last sync is not overwritten; pull lists it and stops unless --force is given. Pull updates the revision in published.json.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Compares the local package with GetPackage: files changed locally, files changed in the academy, and both. It also includes course-spec's lesson status, so a lesson changed since its video was published is reported.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The SDK returns *academyos.APIError for non-2xx responses:

type APIError struct {
    Status   int
    Code     string             // such as "stale_revision", "invalid_course", "unauthorized"
    Message  string
    Findings []validate.Finding // server validation, in course-spec's format
    Changed  []string           // for stale_revision: paths changed in the academy
}

The server's error body is {"code": "...", "message": "...", "findings": [...], "changed": [...]}.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
academyos whoami
academyos course validate <dir> [--strict-narration]
academyos course status <dir>
academyos course push <dir> [--dry-run] [--prune] [--force]
academyos course pull <dir> [--force]
academyos course publish <dir>
academyos version

Global flags: --api-url, --org, --format text|json.

Exit codes:

Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Failure: network, server, or usage 2 The course has validation errors, locally or on the server 3 Stale copy: pull first, or force 4 Authentication or permission failure

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Unit tests against an httptest server that implements the endpoints above, including missing-file rounds, conflicts, and errors.
  • coursepkg tests over course-spec's test course, including a shared theme outside the course directory.
  • A test that fails if any package in go list -deps is from the AcademyOS server module.
